primitives.name: Correlated Random Walk
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Increments {X_n} form a 2-state Markov chain (symmetric case: P(stay)=p=q).
primitives.latex: P(X_{n+1} = x | X_n = y) = \begin{cases} p & \text{if } x = y \\ 1-p & \text{if } x = -y \end{cases}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X_n': 'random walk increment, ±1', 'p': 'probability of staying in same state, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Binary increments, memoryless transition structure, symmetric probabilities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As p → 1, the walk becomes deterministic; as p → 0.5, it approximates i.i.d. behavior.

layer2.mapping: Models clustered outcomes in betting systems where consecutive wins or losses occur more frequently than under independence.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that standard ruin theory assumes independent increments, which fails in real-world betting due to clustering of wins/losses. By modeling increments as a 2-state Markov chain, we derive a closed-form ruin probability α that depends on the persistence parameter p. When p > 0.5, the effective ruin probability increases compared to i.i.d. models because long streaks amplify drawdown risk. The martingale approach allows us to compute both ruin probability and expected duration using OST. The key innovation lies in adapting this framework to variable Kelly stakes and multi-state extensions. The failure mode occurs when p approaches 1, leading to near-deterministic paths and numerical instability in the ruin formula. Additionally, the assumption of unit stakes limits direct application to GSE’s variable-stake environment unless extended via scaling arguments.
